prompt:
ONE original square premium painterly cinematic Mitoloka illustration of the Mohan, the heavily haired corpulent Colombian river spirit.
ANATOMY: ONE very CORPULENT human-like figure, ONE head, TWO natural eyes, TWO arms and TWO legs; abundant LONG UNKEMPT dark HAIR covers much of torso, shoulders and legs, long tangled beard almost merging with body hair. Broad weathered face half-hidden by filthy wet strands, fully opaque coarse dark chest cloth and waist wrap beneath hair, no nudity. No horns, hooves, animal head or invented giant scale [mohan-legendary-c10].
MOMENT: Haul a stolen empty fishing NET violently backward into a riverside cave, both thick hands gripping the wet net as it stretches toward foreground, body braced and head turning with a ferocious glare directly toward viewer. Water pours from real net knots, one bare foot braces on wet rock.
POWER: steals fishermen's nets, no visible magic or water-control effects [mohan-legendary-c07].
SCALE & CAMERA: extreme low close angle at river edge, hairy corpulent head/shoulders and net-pulling arms fill square, normal human-like size through framing, no tiny people comparator.
LIGHT & WEATHER: one low amber moon shaft catches wet hair and strained net fibres, deep walnut cave shadows, ordinary river spray and humidity.
SURFACE: matted wet long body hair, thick dirty beard, weathered skin, coarse opaque wrap, muddy rope fishing net, slick cave stone.
SETTING: Colombian jungle river with a dark waterside cave at night [mohan-legendary-c11].
MOOD: dangerous uncanny river spirit caught in forceful net theft, never ordinary fisherman, cute hairy mascot or calm portrait. No victims, fish injury, gore or glowing aura.
HARD CONSTRAINTS: no text, lettering, inscriptions, logo, border, frame or watermark; no extra heads, limbs or fingers; no design borrowed from any film, game, anime or comic; no nudity or explicit gore; no generic glow aura, neon outline or energy ribbons. Premium painterly brushwork, dark warm walnut and antique gold palette, square composition.
name: Mohan (legendary)
rationale: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.

visual_review.notes: Native and 200px inspected: one very bulky corpulent human-like figure with unusually abundant long unkempt hair covering torso/shoulders/legs and thick beard; two hands strain empty net, foot braced at cave. Opaque wrap visible under hair, no nudity. Forceful net theft, confrontational gaze and extreme hair silhouette remain uncanny at thumbnail, not relaxed fisherman. No horns/hooves/watermagic, victims, text or aura. Seven Sangar checks pass.

root_visual_review.notes: Viewed native 1254px, 200px, and face, both-hand, foot, hip and lower-left crops. One very corpulent humanlike figure (mohan-legendary-c10) with one head, two eyes in a hard glare at the viewer, and a heavy tangled beard. Abundant long, wet, unkempt hair pours over his head, shoulders, arms, torso and legs, covering much of his body (c10). An opaque coarse brown wrap covers the hips, and the groin is hidden behind the wrap, hair and net, so there is no nudity. Two arms: both hands (thumb plus four fingers where visible) violently haul a stolen fishing net with floats backward (steals fishermen's nets, c07). Two legs: the near bare foot, with five toes, braces on wet rock, and the far foot shows faintly through the net at lower left. He drags the net into a dark waterside cave by a moonlit jungle river at night (c11), with water streaming from it. No victims, captives, satyr parts, shapeshift or aura. The sheer hairy bulk, the glare and the forceful theft read as an uncanny river spirit, not an ordinary fisherman, at 200px. No text.
